paper_metadata.title: Ultrastrong High-Ductility Ni35Co35Fe10Al10Ti8B2 High-Entropy Alloy Strengthened with Super-High Concentration L12 Precipitates

evidence.quote: Herein, a novel high-entropy alloy (HEA) Ni35Co35Fe10Al8Ti10B2 with ultrahigh concentration L12 precipitates is successfully designed aided by the calculation of phase diagrams (CALPHAD).
Ni35Co35Fe10Al10Ti8B2 HEA

process_steps.input_state: elemental Ni, Co, Fe, Ti, Al, B (>99.9 wt% purity)
process_steps.output_state: as-cast button ingot (~30 mm diameter, ~10 mm height)

evidence.quote: prepared by the arc-melting method in a water-cooled copper crucible under a highly pure Ar atmosphere, using Ni, Co, Fe, Ti, Al, and B with purities >99.9 wt%. All the ingots were melted at least 6 times to ensure uniform composition. The resulting cast ingots were button shaped with a diameter of approximately 30 mm and a height of approximately 10 mm.
Then, the as-cast samples were homogenized at 1423 K for 2 h followed by water quenching to room temperature.
Cold rolling was carried out with a total thickness reduction of 75%.
Subsequently, the cold-rolled sheet was partial recrystallized at 1273 K for 5 min and quenched in water.
Finally, these samples were isothermally aged at 1023 K for 8 h, and water-quenched to room temperature.
As-cast and cold-rolled samples have a single-phase FCC structure, and thermal processing samples exhibit FCC and L12 phases.
The alloy is mainly composed of dendrites of bright FCC and dark L12, where the volume fraction of L12 is about 20%.

The Rietveld refinement result of the thermal processed ATB2 is summarized in Figure S1, Supporting Information, which could accurately detect the proportion of FCC and L12 phases as 20.4% and 79.6%, respectively.
